facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Last-twelve-months issuer-adjusted EBITDA was CAD 1,006 million at Sept. 30, 2026 against CAD 1,104 million for FY2025, a fall of CAD 98 million, while gross debt at carrying value fell only CAD 123 million to CAD 4,220 million. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a weakening credit is liquidity and tenor: no cash is drawn on committed facilities, only about 26% of principal falls due by 2030, and the company reaffirmed its 2026 outlook of CAD 950 million to CAD 1,050 million of adjusted EBITDA, which needs only CAD 191 million in the fourth quarter after CAD 759 million in nine months to reach the low end. If fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA exceeds the CAD 247 million of the fourth quarter of 2025, last-twelve-months EBITDA would rise and the 4.19x gross leverage would ease; weaker Alberta prices, the Colorado debt or further mothballing of Alberta units would push it the other way. facts.text: The business profile is adequate: diversified by technology but dependent on Alberta. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence that the profile is better than adequate is cash generation and guidance: the company reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA of CAD 950 million to CAD 1,050 million, needs only CAD 191 million in the fourth quarter to reach the low end, and paid its dividends from free cash flow with room to spare. If fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA exceeds the CAD 247 million of a year earlier, last-twelve-months EBITDA would rise above CAD 1,006 million, which would ease the 4.19x gross leverage if debt were unchanged. The view would weaken if Alberta prices fall further, if the Colorado project debt proves to be recourse, if the leverage ratio stays above the top of the issuer's target, or if S&P acts on its negative outlook. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings support a credit snapshot of TransAlta Corporation as at the end of Q3 2026, but not an annual FY2025 comparison, instrument-level debt terms or covenant headroom, so creditor conclusions must stay at the level of consolidated leverage, liquidity and operations.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 67–71; 40-F_2025-12-31_tac-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 2

The Form 40-F is only a cover document: the audited statements, annual management discussion and annual information form it incorporates are not supplied, so year-end 2025 appears only as comparatives inside the 2026 interim filings. The three quarterly management discussion exhibits repeat text already inside the combined news releases, so the evidence is four distinct filings, not seven files.
Basis: 40-F_2025-12-31_tac-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; 40-F_2025-12-31_tac-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C05

Debt is known by category and maturity year, not by instrument, and covenants are described only as customary and complied with. The October 2026 acquisition and minority sale fall after the balance sheet date and no pro forma leverage is supplied, so reported period figures and the effect of those transactions cannot be combined.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 87; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 89; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 39; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 98

TRANSALTA CORP (TransAlta Corporation) as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: the financial foundation for Q3 2026 against FY2025: statements, carrying-value debt, net debt, liquidity, maturities, issuer-adjusted EBITDA leverage and cover, and events after the Sept. 30, 2026 balance sheet.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage on issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose to 4.19x gross and 3.85x net at the end of Q3 2026 from 3.93x and 3.75x at year-end 2025, because EBITDA fell faster than debt, while liquidity of CAD 1,867 million covers scheduled maturities through 2027 more than four times.
Basis: calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C17; calculation C18

Nine-month issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 3.80x cash interest paid, and the Sept. 30, 2026 balance sheet excludes the October 2026 Colorado acquisition, which brings US$750 million of assumed project debt, with no pro forma leverage stated.
Basis: calculation C11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 98
### Key findings

Last-twelve-months issuer-adjusted EBITDA was CAD 1,006 million at Sept. 30, 2026 against CAD 1,104 million for FY2025, a fall of CAD 98 million, while gross debt at carrying value fell only CAD 123 million to CAD 4,220 million. The EBITDA fall is the same CAD 98 million nine-month decline: the Energy Transition segment, where Centralia stopped coal generation, lost CAD 90 million and Hydro lost CAD 48 million, partly offset by Gas, which gained CAD 32 million. Hydro and Gas revenues fell on lower Alberta spot and ancillary prices, net of favourable hedge pricing, while debt service is fixed, so leverage rises when merchant earnings soften.

Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 12

Net debt fell CAD 263 million to CAD 3,875 million because cash rose CAD 140 million to CAD 345 million and no cash is drawn on the committed credit facilities, against CAD 95 million drawn at year-end. The June 2026 share offering raised CAD 338 million net and was used partly to repay those drawings, so the improvement came from new equity rather than from earnings; the offering was raised to fund the cash price of the Colorado acquisition, which was paid after the balance sheet date. The issuer's own leverage measure, which adds half of its preferred shares, was 4.1x against a long-term target of 3.0x to 4.0x.

Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 92; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 98

Nine-month issuer-adjusted EBITDA of CAD 759 million was 3.80x cash interest paid of CAD 200 million, and a twelve-month cover cannot be built because FY2025 cash interest paid is not supplied. Interest expense fell to CAD 241 million from CAD 266 million after 2025 refinancings at lower rates, which supports cover, but the CAD 98 million fall in EBITDA is nearly four times the CAD 25 million interest saving.

Basis: calculation C11; calculation C18; calculation C26; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 67; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 71

Liquidity of CAD 1,867 million is cash of CAD 345 million plus CAD 1,522 million of undrawn committed capacity after letters of credit issued under both committed and non-committed lines; the syndicated and bilateral committed lines were extended in July 2026 to 2030 and 2028. Scheduled debt maturities are CAD 54 million in the rest of 2026 and CAD 338 million in 2027, and CAD 3,150 million falls after 2030, including CAD 750 million of exchangeable securities that Brookfield may convert but cannot call for repayment. The working capital deficit of CAD 219 million is mainly that exchangeable line classed as current.

Basis: calculation C12; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C26; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 87–89

Two events after the balance sheet date are kept out of every period figure. On Oct. 22, 2026 the company closed the Colorado gas acquisition for US$1.0 billion including US$750 million of assumed project debt, and sold a 49 per cent interest in its Oklahoma wind portfolio for US$305 million of cash. Net debt and leverage after both are not established because the sources state no exchange rate and no pro forma figure.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 98; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weakening credit is liquidity and tenor: no cash is drawn on committed facilities, only about 26% of principal falls due by 2030, and the company reaffirmed its 2026 outlook of CAD 950 million to CAD 1,050 million of adjusted EBITDA, which needs only CAD 191 million in the fourth quarter after CAD 759 million in nine months to reach the low end. If fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA exceeds the CAD 247 million of the fourth quarter of 2025, last-twelve-months EBITDA would rise and the 4.19x gross leverage would ease; weaker Alberta prices, the Colorado debt or further mothballing of Alberta units would push it the other way.

Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C27; calculation C28; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Limitations

- No audited FY2025 statements are supplied, so FY2025 income and cash flow lines other than three stated headline figures are not established and no twelve-month cash interest or reported EBITDA can be built.
- The issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA, so leverage and cover use the issuer-adjusted measure and are labelled as such.
- The debt table gives categories and a maturity ladder, not instruments, so coupons, security, guarantors and call dates are not established.
- US dollar amounts of the October 2026 transactions are not converted, because no rate is stated.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Governance and ownership risk looks moderate, but the business carries Alberta merchant-price exposure and execution risk on the Centralia conversion and data-centre plans, so creditors rely on contracted and hedged cash flow and on growth that is only partly equity-funded.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 25

Alberta supplies 51.6% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA and 77% of Alberta capacity is exposed to the merchant market, while 53% of total capacity is contracted with a weighted average life of 9 years. Five senior roles changed in 2026, the cash price of the Colorado acquisition was paid with new equity, and the dividend rose 8% with no documented debt-funded distribution.

Basis: calculation C01; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 25; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-05-06_q12026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-07-31_q22026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Key findings

The profit pool is diversified by technology but concentrated in Alberta and gas. Gas earned CAD 374 million of the CAD 759 million nine-month adjusted EBITDA and Alberta CAD 392 million, so Alberta spot and ancillary prices drive results even though the fleet spans hydro, wind, solar and gas across Canada, the United States and Western Australia. A hedge position priced at $67 per MWh covers part of fourth-quarter 2026 Alberta production, which dampens but does not remove the exposure.
Basis: calculation C01; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25

Management continuity is orderly but thin on history. The chief executive retired on April 30, 2026 and was succeeded by the chief financial officer, a new chief financial officer and chief commercial officer followed within a week, and two further senior roles changed on June 8, 2026. Four independent directors, all audit committee financial experts, sit on the audit committee, and internal control was assessed as effective at Sept. 30, 2026 excluding the Far North acquisition.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-05-06_q12026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-07-31_q22026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5; 40-F_2025-12-31_tac-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67

Capital allocation has been acquisitive and partly equity-funded, not extractive. The June 2026 offering of about CAD 350 million funded the cash price of the Colorado acquisition, the Far North purchase of CAD 107 million used cash and credit facilities, the 49 per cent Oklahoma wind sale for US$305 million brings in cash, and no shares were repurchased in 2026 against CAD 24 million in the first nine months of 2025. The trade-off is project debt of US$750 million assumed with Colorado and an 8% higher dividend.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-07-31_q22026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 70; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 77; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 98

No sponsor controls the company on the evidence supplied, but holder percentages are not established. Brookfield holds CAD 750 million of exchangeable securities, made up of CAD 350 million of 7% debentures due 2039 and CAD 400 million of preferred shares; they are exchangeable into the Alberta Hydro Assets at its option, it cannot call for repayment, and it may nominate two directors. A related-party power sale to Brookfield was small and fell in the first quarter of 2026.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-05-06_q12026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 72; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-05-06_q12026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 93; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 88

Execution and regulatory risk sit in three projects. The Centralia unit has had no generation in 2026 and runs under repeated 90-day federal orders whose costs are excluded from adjusted EBITDA and not yet recovered, the conversion needs about US$600 million of capital with a decision expected in early 2027, and the Alberta data-centre plans depend on approvals and definitive agreements while four thermal units are mothballed or notified for mothballing.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 32; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 44; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 64–65; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-05-06_q12026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a lower-risk reading is financial discipline: the cash price of the main acquisition was equity-funded, no extraction is documented, Brookfield's capital cannot be called, and the committed credit lines were extended in July 2026. The moderate rating would move higher if the Colorado project debt proves non-recourse and the data-centre agreement becomes a binding long-term contract, and lower if a debt-funded distribution, a further large acquisition without equity, or a failed Centralia approval appeared. Ownership percentages and creditor documents would also change it.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 40; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 98; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-05-06_q12026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Limitations
- The annual information form is not supplied, so the finding that no sponsor controls the company could change if a large holder or control right exists outside the interim filings.
- No credit agreement or indenture is supplied, so the finding that no creditor-adverse behaviour is documented is not tested against restricted-payment, investment or asset-transfer capacity.
- The Colorado project debt terms are not stated, so whether the acquisition adds recourse debt, and how much it weakens the equity-funded-growth finding, is not established.
- Management and board history beyond the 2026 appointments is not supplied, so the continuity finding rests on appointment dates alone.

| Fleet | 89 facilities with 8,623 MW of gross installed capacity: hydro 922 MW, wind and solar 2,587 MW, gas 5,114 MW. | Gas is 59% of capacity and 49% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA, so gas margins matter most. | 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 12 |

| Other senior roles | Nancy Brennan, Chief Legal, People and Corporate Affairs Officer, and Chris Fralick, EVP Generation and Chief Operating Officer, both from June 8, 2026. | 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-07-31_q22026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Four transactions shaped 2026. Far North, four Ontario gas facilities of 310 MW, closed on Feb. 2, 2026 for CAD 95 million, or CAD 107 million with working capital adjustments, paid from cash and credit facility draws. TRANSALTA CORP (TransAlta Corporation) as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: the overall fundamental credit profile, its strongest support, its primary downside path and the signals to monitor, built from the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses and the interim filings to Nov. 3, 2026.

## Findings
### Bottom line

TransAlta's fundamental credit profile is adequate but weakening: leverage on issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose to 4.19x gross and 3.85x net at the end of Q3 2026, while liquidity of CAD 1,867 million and most principal falling due after 2030 keep near-term refinancing risk low. Pro forma net debt and leverage after the Colorado acquisition and Oklahoma wind sale of October 22, 2026 are not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C07

The primary downside path is a further fall in Alberta merchant earnings: nine-month adjusted EBITDA already fell CAD 98 million, and the Colorado acquisition adds US$750 million of assumed project debt. S&P rates the company BB+ with a negative outlook, and the issuer's own leverage of 4.1x is above its 3.0x to 4.0x target.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04; calculation C11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 38; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 98
### Key findings

The business profile is adequate: diversified by technology but dependent on Alberta. The fleet spans hydro, wind, solar and gas in three countries and 53% of capacity is contracted for a weighted average of 9 years, yet Alberta produced 51.6% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA and 77% of Alberta capacity is exposed to the merchant market, so Alberta prices set the earnings that service debt.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 25

The financial profile is weakening on leverage but stable on liquidity. Last-twelve-months issuer-adjusted EBITDA fell 8.9% to CAD 1,006 million while debt at carrying value fell only 2.8%, so gross leverage rose from 3.93x to 4.19x and net leverage from 3.75x to 3.85x; these figures exclude the October 22, 2026 Colorado acquisition and Oklahoma wind sale, and pro forma net debt after them is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05

Interest cover is moderate rather than thin. Nine-month issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 3.80x cash interest paid, and free cash flow of CAD 338 million covered the CAD 100 million of common and preferred dividends paid 3.4 times, leaving CAD 238 million after dividends. A twelve-month cover is not available because full-year 2025 cash interest paid is not supplied.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C08; calculation C09; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71

Liquidity and refinancing risk are low in the near term. Liquidity of CAD 1,867 million is more than four times the CAD 392 million of principal due by the end of 2027, no cash is drawn on committed facilities, and the syndicated and bilateral facilities were extended in July 2026. Instrument-level terms and covenant levels are not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40

Governance and sponsor risk is moderate. The cash price of the Colorado acquisition was paid with new equity, the dividend rose 8% and no extraction is documented, but five senior roles changed in 2026 and ownership percentages and debt documents are not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-05-06_q12026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-07-31_q22026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence that the profile is better than adequate is cash generation and guidance: the company reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA of CAD 950 million to CAD 1,050 million, needs only CAD 191 million in the fourth quarter to reach the low end, and paid its dividends from free cash flow with room to spare. If fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA exceeds the CAD 247 million of a year earlier, last-twelve-months EBITDA would rise above CAD 1,006 million, which would ease the 4.19x gross leverage if debt were unchanged. The view would weaken if Alberta prices fall further, if the Colorado project debt proves to be recourse, if the leverage ratio stays above the top of the issuer's target, or if S&P acts on its negative outlook.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10; calculation C14; calculation C15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 38
### Limitations

- Debt terms are known only by category and maturity year, so the view that refinancing risk is low rests on maturity totals and could change if specific instruments carry calls, security or covenants not shown.
- Covenant levels are not supplied, so the liquidity view cannot be tested against headroom and could weaken if a financial covenant is closer than the compliance statement implies.
- The pro forma effect of the Colorado debt and the Oklahoma sale is not established, so the leverage trend could improve or worsen after October 22, 2026.
- Audited FY2025 statements are not supplied, so the weakening-leverage conclusion compares a twelve-month figure with a year-end headline figure rather than audited annual statements.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: liquidity and bank support. Cash of CAD 345 million and undrawn committed capacity of CAD 1,522 million give CAD 1,867 million of liquidity, no cash is drawn on committed facilities, and the July 2026 extensions to 2030 and 2028 remove near-term bank maturity risk, so a price shock would meet a large buffer.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40

Strength: a diversified, partly contracted fleet. Gas, wind and solar, hydro and marketing earn separately, 53% of capacity is contracted, and hedges are priced at $65 per MWh for 2027, which narrows the range of near-term cash flow.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 24

Strength: growth funded partly with equity. New equity paid the cash price of the Colorado acquisition and about 74% of principal falls due after 2030, although the Colorado project debt is not in that maturity ladder.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07

Weakness: leverage above the issuer's target and rising. The issuer measures 4.1x against a 3.0x to 4.0x target, and the 4.19x gross and 3.85x net ratios on issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose in 2026 because EBITDA fell faster than debt, which leaves little room for a further earnings fall before ratings pressure builds.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41

Weakness: merchant earnings and execution risk. Alberta provides 51.6% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA with 77% of its capacity merchant, Centralia has no generation under repeated federal orders, and four thermal units are mothballed or notified for mothballing while data-centre demand is unproven.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 12

Weakness: opaque debt terms. Covenant levels, instrument ranking, guarantors and the recourse of the US$750 million of Colorado project debt are not supplied, so creditor protection cannot be judged beyond the consolidated figures.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
